title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: The best investment decisions are made when you steelman your opponent's thesis better than they can, price the probabilities honestly, and refuse to deploy capital until the tape confirms your edge.
epigraph.author: Institutional Capital Allocation Playbook

web_blocks.html: Every durable investment call requires weighing both sides of the aisle without cheerleading management or succumbing to headline panic. On the Bull side, Uber has completed a rare structural transformation: Gross Bookings compound at ~20% YoY ($193.5B in FY2025; $59.82B in Q3 2026), GAAP Operating Income doubled to $5,565 million in FY2025, and Free Cash Flow reached $10.4 billion TTM on just 0.6% capex intensity [2, 3, 21]. High-margin Advertising (> $2.5B annualized run-rate) and Uber One (>50M members driving >50% of Mobility+Delivery bookings) deepen consumer lock-in, while $10.8 billion in 2025–9M 2026 share buybacks shrinks the diluted share count [3, 9, 19]. In an autonomous future, bulls argue that fleet utilization—not vehicle manufacturing—is the scarce economic bottleneck, positioning Uber as the indispensable demand aggregator for Waymo, Aurora, and regional AV operators [16, 18].

On the Bear side, the Skeptic case is grounded in three tangible risks flagged in our `PASS_WITH_WATCH` KPI audit [15, 16, 22]. First, if Waymo or Tesla achieve dense autonomous fleet scale in top-20 U.S. metros and build direct consumer habit without relying on Uber's app, Uber's ~28%–30% Mobility take rate could compress toward software-routing levels, capping terminal FCF multiples [16, 18]. Second, U.S. commercial auto insurance inflation continues to pressure Mobility cost of revenue [14]. Third, UK VAT merchant-of-record (TOMS) reform creates a structural optical drag on reported Mobility revenue and margins [15]. Layered atop a broader US market Downtrend (42.6% breadth >50DMA, 7 distribution days, 5.12% 10Y yield) and UBER's Stage 4 technical breakdown below $71.94–$72.55, bears argue the multiple can compress further to 10x–11x FCF before fundamentals force a re-rating [21, 23, 24].

web_blocks.html: Our independent synthesis weighs both sides against probability-weighted cash-flow math. At $68.81, our Bear case ($52.00, 25% weight) models AV take-rate compression, auto insurance inflation, and UK VAT drag, de-rating shares to ~10.5x FCF. Our Base case ($88.00, 55% weight) models 14%–16% Gross Bookings growth, >$3.5B in Advertising, and hybrid AV partnerships lifting the multiple to 16x FCF. Our Bull case ($108.00, 20% weight) models 25%+ AV dispatch share and >4% annual share retirements. Those weights produce an $83.00 expected value (+20.6% vs. CMP). Even so, Stage 4 technicals and a US Downtrend forbid buying at $68.81. Waiting for $62.00–$65.00 support creates a 3.54:1 entry (($88.00 - $65.00) / ($65.00 - $58.50)) with a hard $58.50 stop [21, 23, 24].

What Changes Our Verdict: Upgrade from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to active buy if UBER stabilizes in the $62.00–$65.00 shelf with a 4H higher low, or reclaims $73.50 on ≥1.25x volume as S&P 500 breadth exits Downtrend. Downgrade to REJECTED if UBER breaks $58.50 alongside rising AV take-rate compression.

This discipline keeps portfolio risk tightly controlled. We never average down into a Stage 4 breakdown or force cash into weak setups. By waiting for proven demand at $62.00–$65.00, we protect our $3,818.88 cash reserve and preserve 3.54:1 upside.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the final chapter, where all of our business forensics, valuation math, and chart discipline converge into a single, unambiguous action plan. To make a decision you can stick with through volatility, you and I must first steelman both sides of the debate without cheerleading management or surrendering to headline panic.

On the Bull side, Uber has evolved into one of the cleanest cash-compounding marketplaces in global technology. Across FY2025 and Q3 2026, Gross Bookings compounded at roughly 20% year-over-year—reaching $193.5 billion in FY2025 and $59.82 billion in Q3 2026—while GAAP Operating Income doubled to $5,565 million in FY2025 and trailing twelve-month Free Cash Flow hit $10.4 billion on just 0.6% capital expenditure intensity. High-margin Advertising has scaled past a $2.5 billion annualized run-rate, Uber One has surpassed 50 million members driving over half of Mobility and Delivery bookings, and management has deployed $10.8 billion into share repurchases across 2025 and the first nine months of 2026. In an autonomous future, bulls argue that fleet utilization—not vehicle manufacturing—is the scarce economic bottleneck, positioning Uber as the indispensable demand aggregator for Waymo, Aurora, and regional AV operators.

On the Bear side, the risks are concrete and deserve full respect. First, if Waymo or Tesla achieve dense autonomous fleet scale in top-20 U.S. metros and cultivate direct consumer habit without relying on Uber's app, Uber's 28% to 30% Mobility take rate could compress toward low-single-digit software routing fees, capping terminal Free Cash Flow multiples. Second, U.S. commercial auto insurance inflation continues to pressure Mobility cost of revenue. Third, UK VAT merchant-of-record (TOMS) reform creates an optical drag on reported Mobility revenue and margins. Layered atop a broader US market Downtrend—with only 42.6% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, 7 distribution days, and a 5.12% 10-year Treasury yield—and Uber's Stage 4 technical breakdown below $71.94–$72.55, bears argue the multiple can compress to 10x–11x FCF before fundamentals force a re-rating.

When we weight those outcomes honestly, we avoid false precision and price the distribution. We assign a 25% probability to our $52.00 Bear case (-24.4% vs. CMP), where autonomous expansion erodes metro take rates and compresses the multiple to ~10.5x FCF. We assign a 55% probability to our $88.00 Base case (+27.9% vs. CMP), where Gross Bookings compound at 14%–16%, Advertising scales past $3.5 billion, and hybrid AV partnerships preserve take rates as the multiple mean-reverts to 16x FCF. And we assign a 20% probability to our $108.00 Bull case (+57.0% vs. CMP), where Uber captures 25%+ of AV dispatch volume and retires over 4% of shares annually. Weighting those scenarios—0.25 times $52 plus 0.55 times $88 plus 0.20 times $108—produces a probability-weighted expected value of $83.00, or +20.6% above today's $68.81 close.

Across our three time horizons, the verdict is crystal clear. For Short-Term Trading and Momentum (1 to 12 weeks), our stance is Avoid / Wait while the stock remains in Stage 4 below its 50-day ($69.31) and 200-day ($72.55) moving averages on elevated down-day volume. For Medium-Term Inflection (3 to 12 months), we assign Wait for Support in the $62.00 to $65.00 zone (or a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above $73.50). For Long-Term Compounding (2 to 5 years), Uber remains a COMPOUNDER_PASS ready to accumulate once support holds.

Look at why waiting for $62.00–$65.00 transforms the math. At the upper edge of our $65.00 entry zone, pairing a $65.00 entry with a hard $58.50 invalidation stop against our $88.00 Base target yields a 3.54-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio (($88.00 minus $65.00) divided by ($65.00 minus $58.50)). Once price tests $64.04 and stabilizes, you can also deploy the defined-risk January 15, 2027 $67.5/$77.5 Bull Call Debit Spread ($3.73 debit, $373.00 max loss, $627.00 max profit, 1.68:1 R:R).

Finally, let us reconcile the existing portfolio. Our consolidated equity ledger holds zero common UBER shares, so our common holding action is NOT_HELD (holding_shares_to_sell: 0). However, the options book carries 5 December 17, 2027 LEAPS contracts—4x $110 calls ($1,307.91 market value) and 1x $100 call ($467.95 market value)—totaling $1,775.86 (2.14% of our $82,808.19 net worth) with 395 days to expiry. We rate both LEAPS lines a disciplined HOLD above the $63.00 invalidation floor. As for our $3,818.88 in marginal cash, we allocate 100% to CASH right now rather than forcing 0% into Microsoft ($506.24, Stage 3 CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT, $660.00 Base target, 4.5:1 asymmetry) or Airbnb ($180.94, CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION, $215.00 Base target, 1.75:1 asymmetry) while the US market remains in a Downtrend.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: PATIENCE AS AN ACTIVE POSITION
book_callouts.text: Sitting in cash while a high-quality compounder finishes a Stage 4 pullback feels uncomfortable, yet it is the highest-return discipline in portfolio management. By refusing to buy at $68.81 and waiting for $62.00–$65.00 support, you transform a 1.6x–2.0x trade into a 3.54:1 asymmetric setup with a clearly defined $58.50 exit.
